2.name: records codicil suspicions
2.description: Asha notes witness testimony about a codicil executed in October, possible drafting attorney identities, the folder's location, and uncertainties about who accessed the desk.
evidence: *Witness recalls codicil executed October. Drafting attorney possibly Stein/Stine — not Halloran. Folder reportedly placed in bottom right drawer of sewing-room desk. Desk has not yet been opened in my presence. Key in lock. Daniel was in house Saturday between funeral and meeting; access unverified but plausible. Daniel insists no later instrument exists. Lucia knows something she has not said. Rosa terminated by Daniel within 24 hours of funeral.*
2.time_hint: October; Saturday; within 24 hours of funeral

2.name: adds beneficiary question
2.description: Asha appends a note framing the central question of who benefits if the codicil appears or disappears.
evidence: Then she added, underneath:
*Question for tomorrow: who benefits from the codicil if it surfaces, and who benefits from it not surfacing, and are those two answers the same.*

2.name: closes investigation notes
2.description: Asha finishes writing, closes the pad, and turns off the kitchen light after reflecting on the house and its occupants.
evidence: She put the pen down. She closed the pad.
Asha turned off the kitchen light.

2.name: lies awake after writing
2.description: Asha does not sleep well that night, having already expected to be unable to rest.
evidence: She did not sleep well. She had not expected to.

2.name: arrives with paralegal at house
2.description: At 9:45 the next morning, Asha stands on the sidewalk in front of the house with her paralegal Marcus, who brings equipment for the visit.
evidence: At nine forty-five the next morning she was on the sidewalk in front of the house with her paralegal, a quiet young man named Marcus who carried a banker's box and a digital camera and asked no questions he had not been asked to ask.
2.location_hint: sidewalk in front of the house

2.name: Asha arrives with legal team
2.description: Asha arrives at the house with her paralegal Marcus, who carries evidence-gathering supplies.
evidence: sidewalk in front of the house with her paralegal, a quiet young man named Marcus who carried a banker's box and a digital camera
The day was bright and cold.
2.location_hint: sidewalk in front of the house

2.name: Rosa stores the umbrella away
2.description: The umbrella that had been in the vestibule is no longer there because Rosa has put it away.
evidence: The umbrella was no longer in the brass stand inside the vestibule; Rosa had put it away.

2.name: Lucia admits Daniel is upstairs
2.description: Lucia opens the door and tells Asha that Daniel is already in the house and has gone up to the sewing room.
evidence: Lucia opened the door this time
"He's already here."
"How long?"
"Twenty minutes. He went up to the sewing room."

2.name: Lucia confirms Daniel stayed at doorway
2.description: Lucia reassures Asha that she followed Daniel and made sure he did not enter the sewing room.
evidence: "By himself?"
"I followed him. He was standing in the doorway. He didn't go in."
"I made sure."
"Thank you."

2.name: Group ascends to sewing room
2.description: Asha leads Lucia, Marcus, and Rosa upstairs toward the sewing room, with Rosa joining from the back garden carrying a thermos.
evidence: They went up the stairs in a small procession: Asha first, then Lucia, then Marcus with the box, then — coming in through the kitchen door from the back garden, where she had apparently been waiting — Rosa, in the same navy cardigan, with a thermos.

2.name: Daniel blocks hallway then yields
2.description: Daniel waits at the top of the stairs with folded arms, then steps aside when Asha greets him and asks to proceed.
evidence: At the top of the stairs Daniel was standing in the hallway with his arms folded
"Good morning," Asha said.
"Good morning."
"Shall we."
He stepped aside.

2.name: Asha opens sewing room
2.description: Asha opens the sewing-room door to begin the inspection.
evidence: She opened the sewing-room door.

2.name: Asha unlocks roll-top desk
2.description: Asha notices the key in the roll-top lock, puts on gloves, turns the key, and opens the desk.
evidence: The key was still in the lock of the roll top.
Asha put on a pair of thin cotton gloves she had brought in her portfolio — theatrical, perhaps, but the theater was the point — and turned the key, and rolled the top up.

2.name: Desk contents are revealed
2.description: The roll-top opens and the wooden slats clatter, revealing the desk's interior as the inspection begins.
evidence: The wooden slats clattered s

2.name: Asha dons gloves and opens desk
2.description: Asha puts on thin cotton gloves, turns the key, and rolls up the desk top to begin her search.
evidence: Asha put on a pair of thin cotton gloves she had brought in her portfolio — theatrical, perhaps, but the theater was the point — and turned the key, and rolled the top up.

2.name: Asha inspects desk contents
2.description: Asha examines the tidy desk surface and its personal papers and objects without touching them.
evidence: The desk surface beneath was tidy. A blotter. A cup of pens. A stack of unopened envelopes from utilities and from Independence Blue Cross. A pair of reading glasses with one earpiece taped. A small framed photograph of a young woman in a wedding dress on the steps of a church, dated 1971 in faded ink along the white border.
Asha did not touch any of it.

2.name: Asha opens bottom drawer
2.description: Asha crouches and opens the bottom right drawer of the desk to continue searching.
evidence: She crouched, and opened the bottom right drawer.

2.name: Asha finds labeled file folders
2.description: Asha finds a set of manila file folders organized by topic in the drawer.
evidence: Inside were file folders, manila, perhaps a dozen, arranged with their tabs facing up. Taxes 2019. Taxes 2020. Taxes 2021. Medicare. Con Edison. House.

2.name: Asha notes missing will folder
2.description: Asha realizes there is no folder labeled as a will or codicil in the drawer.
evidence: There was no folder marked Will or Codicil or anything resembling either.

2.name: Asha reviews house folder
2.description: Asha removes the House folder and finds deeds, a copy of the 2020 will, insurance policies, and a roofer's receipt.
evidence: Asha lifted the House folder out and opened it on top of the desk. Deeds. A copy of the 2020 will. Insurance policies. A receipt from a roofer dated 2018. She set it aside.

2.name: Marcus photographs folders
2.description: Marcus documents each folder as Asha goes through them.
evidence: She went through the other folders, one by one, with Marcus photographing each as she opened it.

2.name: Family watches search silently
2.description: Daniel, Lucia, and Rosa observe the search from different positions without intervening.
evidence: Daniel stood in the doorway with his arms still folded. Lucia stood behind him. Rosa stood by the window, looking out at the brick wall, her hand resting lightly on top of the sewing machine the way another woman might have rested her hand on the head of a dog.

2.name: Search yields no codicil
2.description: The search confirms that no codicil is present in the drawer or the other folders.
evidence: There was no codicil in the drawer.
There was no codicil in any of the

2.name: finds no codicil in drawer
2.description: Asha searches the drawer and discovers that the codicil is not there.
evidence: There was no codicil in the drawer.

2.name: checks all drawers for codicil
2.description: Asha expands her search and confirms that none of the drawers contain the codicil.
evidence: There was no codicil in any of the drawers.

2.name: suppresses growing dread
2.description: Asha keeps her expression neutral while feeling a cold, growing weight of realization inside her.
evidence: Asha sat back on her heels. She kept her face neutral. She felt, behind her sternum, the small cold weight of the thing she had filed there the day before, and she felt it begin to grow.

2.name: asks about missing folder
2.description: Asha asks Rosa to clarify what kind of folder the missing document was in.
evidence: "Rosa," she said quietly. "You said the folder. Was it manila, like these, or something else?"

2.name: identifies green important papers folder
2.description: Rosa explains that the missing folder was green and used for the deceased woman's important papers.
evidence: "It was green. A green folder, the kind with a pocket on the inside. The señora bought a box of them at the Staples on Broad Street. She used them for what she called the *important* papers. Medical directive. Funeral instructions. The will."

2.name: learns green folders were stored in drawer
2.description: Rosa says there were several green folders in the drawer while the señora was alive.
evidence: "Were there other green folders in this drawer when she was alive?"
"Three. Maybe four."

2.name: discovers green folders missing
2.description: Asha checks the drawer and realizes that all of the green folders are gone from the drawers she has opened.
evidence: Asha looked at the drawer again. There were no green folders. There were no green folders in any of the drawers she had opened.

2.name: confronts Daniel about folders
2.description: Asha stands and directly asks Daniel where the green folders are.
evidence: She stood up. Her knees clicked. She turned, slowly, and looked at Daniel.
"Mr. Serrano," she said.
"Where are the green folders."

2.name: Daniel withholds answer
2.description: Daniel does not answer immediately, and his posture shifts from authority to self-protection.
evidence: He did not answer at once. His arms were still folded but the fold had changed, had become less a posture of authority and more the posture of a man holding himself together at the ribs.

2.name: Daniel denies knowledge
2.description: Daniel tells Asha he does not know what she is talking about.
evidence: "I don't know what you're talking about," he said.

2.name: Asha confronts Daniel about missing folders
2.description: Asha states that Rosa said Daniel's mother kept important papers in green folders and points out that none are in the desk or room.
evidence: "Green folders," Asha said.
"Rosa says your mother kept her important papers in green folders. There are no green folders in this desk. There are no green folders in this room."

2.name: Daniel suggests his mother moved the papers
2.description: Daniel speculates that his mother may have moved the folders herself.
evidence: "Maybe she moved them."

2.name: Asha presses Daniel for the papers' location
2.description: Asha challenges Daniel to explain where the missing papers could have been moved.
evidence: "Where?"
"When were you last in this room, Mr. Serrano?"

2.name: Daniel admits being in the room after the funeral
2.description: After a measured pause, Daniel says he was last in the room on the day of the funeral before the family returned to the house.
evidence: "The day of the funeral. Before everyone came back to the house. I came up to — I don't know. To stand somewhere alone."

2.name: Daniel denies opening the desk
2.description: Daniel says he did not open the desk when he was alone in the room.
evidence: "Did you open the desk."
"No."

2.name: Daniel denies opening any drawers
2.description: Daniel further denies opening any of the desk drawers.
evidence: "Did you open any of these drawers."
"No."

2.name: Lucia reacts silently
2.description: Lucia makes a suppressed sound behind Daniel, suggesting amusement or disbelief, and Daniel briefly turns toward her before facing Asha again.
evidence: "Lucia made a small sound behind him. Not a word. Something between a breath and the beginning of a laugh that had been amputated before it could become one. Daniel turned his head a quarter inch toward her, did not complete the turn, and faced Asha again."

2.name: Daniel insists he stayed only briefly
2.description: Daniel reiterates that he came upstairs to be alone, sat on a stool for ten minutes, and then returned downstairs without touching his mother's papers.
evidence: "I came up here to be alone," he said. "I sat on that stool for ten minutes. I went back downstairs. I did not touch my mother's papers."

2.name: Asha dismisses Daniel's statement
2.description: Asha responds with a flat, weightless thank-you that signals skepticism rather than gratitude.
evidence: "Thank you," Asha said. She let the thank-you carry no weight at all.

2.name: Asha dismisses the apology lightly
2.description: Asha thanks the speaker in a deliberately weightless way, signaling that she is not granting the apology much significance.
evidence: "Thank you," Asha said. She let the thank-you carry no weight at all. It was the lightest possible acknowledgment, the kind a court reporter might give to a question repeated for the record.

2.name: Asha assigns Marcus desk photography
2.description: Asha instructs Marcus to photograph the desk contents, empty drawers, and rolltop interior for later inventory comparison.
evidence: "Marcus. Please photograph the contents of the desk as they currently stand, and the empty drawers, and the interior of the rolltop. We'll inventory what's here against the executor's list this afternoon."
"Yes, ma'am."

2.name: Asha asks Rosa to search the house
2.description: Asha asks Rosa to accompany her through the rest of the house and identify any place Mrs. Serrano may have hidden a green folder.
evidence: "Rosa. Would you walk through the rest of the house with me and point out anywhere else Mrs. Serrano might have kept a green folder."

2.name: Rosa withdraws from Daniel
2.description: Rosa silently removes her hand from the sewing machine and passes Daniel without looking at him, a gesture that visibly wounds him.
evidence: Rosa nodded once and lifted her hand from the sewing machine. The lifting was slow, as if she were taking her hand off something living.

She passed Daniel in the doorway without looking at him, which was perhaps the most cutting thing Asha had seen any person in this house do to any other person, and Daniel felt it; she saw him feel it; she watched the small muscle along his jaw move and resettle.

2.name: Asha invites Lucia to join the search
2.description: In the hallway, Asha asks Lucia to come with them as they continue searching the house.
evidence: In the hallway Asha turned to Lucia. "Would you come with us."
"Yes."

2.name: Daniel insists on searching together
2.description: Daniel objects to being left in the hallway and insists that if the house is being searched, everyone should search together.
evidence: "All of us," Daniel said. His voice had gotten a little hard at the edges. "If we're searching the house we're searching the house together. I'm not going to stand in the hallway while my sister and the housekeeper give the lawyer a tour."
"Of course," Asha said.

2.name: Group begins house search
2.description: The four of them move through the house together in an awkward line, with Rosa leading the search.
evidence: They went through the house in a slow, awkward four-person line. Rosa led.

2.name: Rosa moves through house familiarly
2.description: Rosa navigates the rooms with intimate familiarity, suggesting she knows the house as if it were part of her own body.
evidence: Rosa led. She moved through the rooms the way a person moves through her own body, with no need t

2.name: accepts the tour
2.description: Asha agrees to continue the house tour.
evidence: "Of course," Asha said.

2.name: guides visitors through the house
2.description: Rosa leads Asha and Marcus through the house in a slow, awkward line.
evidence: They went through the house in a slow, awkward four-person line. Rosa led.

2.name: reveals empty family folders
2.description: In the dining room, Rosa shows three green folders that contain keepsakes rather than legal documents.
evidence: The dining room, where the matriarch had kept a small lacquered box on the sideboard, in which Rosa now showed them three green folders, all empty of anything resembling a legal document — one held photographs from a 1987 trip to Puerto Rico, one held mass cards from funerals going back to the 1990s, and one held a stack of recipes torn from El Diario.
Asha noted each. Marcus photographed each.

2.name: documents family keepsakes
2.description: Asha observes each folder while Marcus photographs them.
evidence: Asha noted each. Marcus photographed each.

2.name: finds cemetery deed and car title
2.description: In the front parlor, Rosa discovers two more green folders containing a cemetery plot deed and an old car title.
evidence: The front parlor, where Rosa opened a cabinet beneath the bookshelves and found two more green folders, one with a deed for a cemetery plot in Holy Cross and one with the title to a 2009 Toyota Camry that had been sold three years before.

2.name: shows preserved bedroom
2.description: Rosa brings Asha to the matriarch's bedroom, where the bed remains made and the slippers are left as if she just stepped out.
evidence: The bedroom on the second floor at the back, the one that had been the matriarch's, where the bed was made and a pair of slippers was placed at angles against the bed-skirt as if their wearer had stepped out of them ten minutes earlier.
2.location_hint: bedroom on the second floor at the back

2.name: refuses to disturb the bed
2.description: Rosa stays in the doorway and tells Asha she did not change the bed because she did not want to.
evidence: Rosa stood in the doorway and did not go in.
"I have not changed the bed," she said quietly, to Asha. "I did not want to."
2.location_hint: bedroom on the second floor at the back

2.name: mentions medical directive folder
2.description: Rosa explains that the matriarch kept her medical directive in the nightstand so paramedics would not have to search for it.
evidence: "In the nightstand," Rosa said. "There was a green folder in the top drawer of the nightstand. She kept her medical directive there. She said if anything happened in the night she did not want the paramedics to have to go looking."
2.location_hint: bedroom on the second floor at the back

2.name: locate missing medical directive
2.description: Asha learns that the green folder containing the medical directive should have been in the top drawer of the nightstand but is missing.
evidence: there was a green folder in the top drawer of the nightstand. She kept her medical directive there.
She said if anything happened in the night she did not want the paramedics to have to go looking.

2.name: inspect empty nightstand drawer
2.description: Asha opens the nightstand drawer and finds personal items but no green folder.
evidence: Asha crossed the room.
The drawer slid open with the small reluctance of old runners.
Inside: a rosary, a tube of hand cream, a paperback novel in Spanish with a bookmark a third of the way through, a flashlight, two AA batteries loose and rolling, and no folder of any color.

2.name: question last sighting of directive
2.description: Asha asks Rosa when she last saw the medical directive in the drawer.
evidence: "Rosa," she said, "when did you last see the medical directive in this drawer."

2.name: confirm directive was present days earlier
2.description: Rosa says she last saw the medical directive three days before the woman died and had read it to her then.
evidence: "Three days before she died."
"I read it to her. She asked me to. She wanted to make sure it said what she remembered it saying."
"And it did."
"It did."

2.name: ask about the will
2.description: Asha shifts the questioning to whether the deceased woman said anything about the will.
evidence: "Did she say anything that day about the will."

2.name: relay instruction about green folder
2.description: Rosa reports that the deceased woman instructed her to ensure the green folder in the desk went to the lawyer first.
evidence: "She said, Rosa, when the time comes, make sure the green folder in the desk goes to the lawyer first. Before anyone else opens the desk."
"I told her I would."

2.name: discover desk already opened
2.description: Rosa says that the morning after the death she found the desk drawer already open and the folder missing.
evidence: "On the morning after she died I went to the desk and the drawer was already open. The folder was not there."

2.name: suspect Lucia took folder
2.description: Rosa initially thinks Lucia may have taken the missing folder.
evidence: "I thought perhaps Lucia had taken it."

2.name: find Lucia at kitchen table
2.description: Rosa goes to the kitchen and sees Lucia sitting at the table with coffee, suggesting she had not taken the folder.
evidence: "I went down to the kitchen and Lucia was at the table with her coffee and she had not"

2.name: checks desk drawer
2.description: The speaker goes to the desk and finds the drawer already open.
evidence: went to the desk and the drawer was already open.

2.name: discovers folder missing
2.description: The speaker realizes the folder is gone from the drawer.
evidence: The folder was not there.

2.name: suspects Lucia took folder
2.description: The speaker briefly thinks Lucia may have taken the missing folder.
evidence: I thought perhaps Lucia had taken it.

2.name: finds Lucia in kitchen
2.description: The speaker goes down to the kitchen and sees Lucia sitting at the table with coffee.
evidence: I went down to the kitchen and Lucia was at the table with her coffee

2.name: confirms Lucia stayed downstairs
2.description: The speaker learns Lucia has not been upstairs that morning, ruling her out as the one who took the folder.
evidence: she had not been upstairs yet that morning.
I knew then.

2.name: asks for clarification
2.description: Another speaker asks what the first speaker realized.
evidence: "You knew what."
